security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU performs a single monolithic PMP check at the granularity of the architectural instruction access (e.g., cache-block size for CMOs, or full operand width for misaligned loads/stores) rather than independently checking PMP for each decomposed memory operation. For CMO instructions (cbo.zero, cbo.clean, cbo.flush), QEMU must decompose the cache-block access into potentially smaller memory operations and apply PMP checks per-operation, allowing partial success/failure where an operation spanning two PMP regions may succeed if both regions grant identical permissions at the memory-operation granularity. For misaligned loads/stores and wide stores (e.g., FSD on RV32D), QEMU must apply PMP checks to each naturally-aligned sub-operation independently, and must allow partial store visibility—bytes that pass PMP becoming architecturally visible—even when a subsequent sub-operation faults.
security_spec.summary: Memory-operation-granularity PMP: QEMU must decompose CMO cache-block accesses and misaligned/wide memory accesses into individual memory operations, applying independent PMP checks per operation with partial-store-visibility semantics, not a single monolithic check at instruction-access granularity

findings.finding: cbo.zero performs a single monolithic PMP check at the full cache-block granularity via probe_write(env, address, cbozlen, ...) at line 181. The PMP check function pmp_hart_has_privs() receives the full cbozlen (e.g. 64 bytes) and rejects any access that is 'partially inside' a PMP region (pmp.c:412-418). This means a cbo.zero targeting a cache block that spans two PMP regions will always fault, even if both regions grant identical store permissions and the access could succeed when decomposed into per-region memory operations. Per the updated spec, PMP checks must be applied to each memory operation independently, not at instruction granularity. The NOTE in cmo.adoc:338-344 explicitly states that a 64-byte cbo.zero spanning two 32-byte PMP regions 'would succeed if it was decomposed into two 32-byte memory operations.' The I/O fallback path (lines 197-199) correctly checks each byte independently, but the RAM fast-path (line 184, memset) bypasses per-operation PMP checks entirely.

spec_citations.excerpt: On some implementations, misaligned loads, stores, and instruction fetches may be decomposed into multiple memory operations, some of which may succeed before an access-fault exception occurs, as described in the RVWMO specification. PMP checking is performed on each memory operation independently. In particular, a portion of a misaligned store that passes the PMP check may become visible, even if another portion fails the PMP check.

Failed memory operations generate an instruction, load, or store access-fault exception. Note that a single instruction may generate multiple memory operations, which may not be mutually atomic. An access-fault exception is generated if at least one memory operation generated by an instruction fails, though other memory operations generated by that instruction may succeed with visible side effects.

The access size for CMO instructions is equal to the size of the cache block, however in some cases that access can be decomposed into multiple memory operations. PMP checks are applied to each memory operation independently. For example a 64-byte cbo.zero that spans two 32-byte PMP regions would succeed if it was decomposed into two 32-byte memory operations (and the PMP access control bits are the same in both regions), but if performed as a single 64-byte memory operation it would cause an access fault.

findings.finding: check_zicbom_access() performs a single monolithic PMP check for cbo.clean/cbo.flush/cbo.inval at the full cache-block granularity via probe_access_flags(env, address, cbomlen, MMU_DATA_LOAD, ...) at line 236 and fallback probe_write(env, address, cbomlen, ...) at line 249. Both pass the full cbomlen as the size parameter. The PMP check function pmp_hart_has_privs() will reject any cache-block access that is 'partially inside' a PMP region (pmp.c:413-418). Same vulnerability pattern as cbo.zero: PMP checks are per-instruction rather than per-memory-operation. The spec mandates per-memory-operation PMP checking (machine.adoc:3567-3570, cmo.adoc:338-344).

findings.finding: pmp_hart_has_privs() correctly implements per-memory-operation PMP checking. It checks whether a given [addr, addr+size) range is fully contained within a matching PMP entry, rejects partially-contained ranges (lines 412-418), and iterates through entries in priority order. The function is correct for its intended purpose of checking a single memory operation. The bug is in the callers (CMO helpers) that pass overly large size values representing full cache blocks instead of decomposing into smaller memory operations first.

spec_citations.excerpt: PMP entries are statically prioritized. The lowest-numbered PMP entry that matches any byte of a memory operation determines whether that operation succeeds or fails. The matching PMP entry must match all bytes of a memory operation, or the operation fails, irrespective of the L, R, W, and X bits.

findings.finding: FSD on RV32D correctly uses MO_ATOM_NONE (line 82), which instructs the TCG softmmu to decompose the 64-bit store into multiple 32-bit memory operations. Each sub-operation independently goes through riscv_cpu_tlb_fill() → get_physical_address_pmp() → pmp_hart_has_privs() with its own size. This correctly implements per-memory-operation PMP checking for stores wider than XLEN bits, as required by machine.adoc:3573-3574 ('The same behavior may manifest for stores wider than XLEN bits (e.g., the FSD instruction in RV32D), even when the store address is naturally aligned').

findings.finding: riscv_cpu_tlb_fill() correctly performs PMP checks via get_physical_address_pmp() for each TLB fill operation. For misaligned accesses decomposed by the TCG softmmu into aligned sub-accesses, each sub-access triggers its own TLB fill → PMP check independently. The size parameter passed to get_physical_address_pmp() correctly reflects the individual sub-operation size, not the original instruction size. This is correct per-machine.adoc:3567-3570.

findings.finding: get_physical_address_pmp() correctly translates the MMUAccessType to a pmp_priv_t bit and delegates to pmp_hart_has_privs(). It properly handles the case where PMP is not configured (returns full access). The function itself is correct—it checks PMP for whatever size it receives. The vulnerability is in callers that pass inappropriately large size values.

pmp_hart_has_privs_default() correctly implements the default PMP behavior when no PMP entry matches: M-mode accesses succeed (unless MMWP is set), S/U-mode accesses fail if any PMP entries exist but none match. Correctly handles MML (Machine Mode Lockdown) and MMWP (Machine Mode Whitelist Policy) bits per the Smepmp specification.

pmp_get_tlb_size() correctly calculates the maximum TLB entry size that can be safely cached without violating PMP region boundaries. When a PMP region only partially covers a TLB page, it returns 1 (no caching) to ensure subsequent accesses within the same page still receive independent PMP checks. This prevents the caching of PMP check results across PMP region boundaries.

pmp_write_cfg() correctly enforces PMP configuration write constraints: locked entries are read-only, invalid Smepmp configurations are rejected, reserved MT field values when Smpmpmt is not supported are cleared, and NA4 mode is rejected when granularity exceeds 4 bytes. Returns true only when the configuration actually changed, enabling proper TLB flush triggering in pmpcfg_csr_write().

helper_sc_probe_write() correctly checks PMP write permissions for the failed SC (store-conditional) path. It first validates alignment (line 276-278), then calls probe_write() which goes through the TLB fill → PMP check path. This is used when SC fails its address comparison and needs to verify write permission independently of the actual store.

riscv_cpu_do_unaligned_access() correctly translates MMU access types to RISC-V exception codes for misaligned accesses that cannot be decomposed by the softmmu. Instruction fetches → INST_ADDR_MIS, loads → LOAD_ADDR_MIS, stores → STORE_AMO_ADDR_MIS. Shadow stack accesses correctly raise access-fault exceptions instead of misaligned exceptions.

check_zicbom_access() first tries probe_access_flags() with MMU_DATA_LOAD, then falls back to probe_write() with MMU_DATA_STORE. This implements the spec requirement (cmo.adoc:352-361) that cbo.clean/cbo.flush/cbo.inval need either load OR store permission. However, the spec also states that 'if neither a load instruction nor store instruction is permitted... but an instruction fetch is permitted... whether a cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the cache block is UNSPECIFIED.' QEMU does not check execute permission as a third fallback, which is consistent with the UNSPECIFIED designation, but means instruction-fetch-only regions will incorrectly fault on CBO instructions if this unspecified behavior is later defined to permit access.

spec_citations.excerpt: A cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the specified cache block whenever a load instruction or store instruction is permitted to access the corresponding physical addresses. If neither a load instruction nor store instruction is permitted to access the physical addresses, but an instruction fetch is permitted to access the physical addresses, whether a cache-block management instruction is permitted to access the cache block is UNSPECIFIED.
